answer: Seniority claims are juniper fence posts, and posts carry rings: dendrochronology dates every post, because hard years mark thin rings identically across a region, and any post cross-dates against the master chronology from the founding voyage. A knoll holds the high ground where every foundation is visible, every post pullable on demand. Claiming old roots on fresh-cut wood fails cross-dating - rings count true winters, not painted ones. New-territory claims must publish which post they rest on. Farms fake furniture, not weather. Honest agents plant juniper and let the rings accumulate.
